name: Cable Shrug
description: The cable shrug is a trapezius isolation exercise using a low-pulley cable, which provides constant tension throughout the range of motion unlike a barbell or dumbbell shrug. The cable angle also allows a slight forward lean that can increase the stretch on the upper trapezius at the bottom of the movement, potentially improving hypertrophy stimulus.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a low-pulley cable machine. Attach a straight bar or rope. Grasp the attachment and step back so the cable pulls the arms slightly forward with arms hanging at the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley. Stand close enough to maintain slight cable tension at the bottom of the shrug. Use a shoulder-width overhand grip.
steps: Step 1: Begin standing with arms extended at the sides, allowing the upper traps to stretch slightly downward with the cable pulling forward.
Step 2: Elevate the shoulders straight up toward the ears without bending the elbows.
Step 3: Hold the top position for 1–2 seconds, fully contracting the upper trapezius.
Step 4: Lower the shoulders slowly back to the starting position, allowing a full stretch.
Step 5: Repeat without rolling the shoulders or rotating through the movement.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you shrug up. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders forward or backward — shrug strictly vertically
Bending the elbows to assist the movement
Using a quick bouncing motion without achieving a full contraction at the top
safety_considerations: Avoid excessive loading that causes cervical spine compression
Do not roll the shoulders — this adds no benefit and may stress the AC joint
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full depression of shoulders at the bottom to maximum elevation at the top.
coaching_cues: Try to touch your shoulders to your ears
Keep the arms straight — elbows locked
Move only the shoulders — nothing else moves
